newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Castle says expenses rose in 1996.
newsitem.headline: A.M. Castle says expenses rose in 1996.

text.p: A.M. Castle & Co said 1996 net income was down slightly versus 1995 due to higher business expenses, but said it should continue to benefit from a favorable specialty metals market.

North America's largest industrial distributor of specialty metals Tuesday reported sales for 1996 of $672.6 million, up seven percent from 1995. Net income on the year fell to $26.1 million from $26.8 million in the prior year.

"This decrease is due to a three percent rise in core business operating expenses, reflecting flat pricing in a slightly inflationary environment and higher levels of transaction activity," the company said.

"Looking ahead, Castle should continue to benefit from a favorable market environment for its specialty metals business. In particular, the growing trends among U.S. manufacturers to outsource non-core competencies and to reduce their total number of suppliers create multiple opportunities for us to expand our industry-leading position," said chairman Michael Simpson.
In the December 31 fourth quarter, revenues reached $160.5 million, up nine percent from a year ago, while net income was $6.2 million, down two percent from a year ago.
